plan: Hold the workspace as a single deep-copied dictionary tree; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy.
Implement one depth-first recursive walker yielding (item, depth) in list order; reuse it for word count, marker collection, and outline so traversal order is identical everywhere.
For notes, strip [[?identifier]] marker tokens before counting \b\w+\b word runs; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect marker identifiers from note text plus reference unresolved lists into a set and return them sorted lexicographically.

In move(), perform all validation (string ids, item lookup, container destination, self/descendant cycle check, index bounds) before any mutation, then pop from the source list and insert/append into the destination list, giving failure atomicity by construction.
mechanisms: deep-copied canonical tree with deep-copy export
shared recursive depth-first walker for all read operations
marker-stripping regex word count with reference declared counts
validate-before-mutate atomic move with cycle and bounds checks
